candidates.name: Proyecto_Final_ProgramacionII (Costa Rica ICT tourism forecasting)
candidates.what_it_holds: data/processed/turismo.csv: cleaned dataset of international tourist arrivals to Costa Rica by country of origin and month, 2019-2025, parsed from data/raw/informes_ict/ (original PDF semi-annual reports from Instituto Costarricense de Turismo, ICT). Uses pdfplumber to extract 'Table 1' (international arrivals by country/month) from each ICT PDF; author states annual totals were validated against ICT's official statistical yearbooks and matched exactly. Also pulls Open-Meteo historical daily temperature for Costa Rica as a weather covariate, aggregated monthly. Includes a trained ML model (not committed, file-size excluded). Course project (BD-143 Programación II), last updated 17 Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Direct, verified LatAm regional travel-volume data (gap #7) with a repeatable, source-checked extraction method (ICT PDF -> table) an agent could re-run on newer ICT reports; monthly, by-origin-country granularity is finer than most public Costa Rica tourism series and could proxy US-outbound leisure travel strength relevant to ABNB's LatAm segment.

candidates.name: Hawaii Tourism Length-of-Stay Analysis Project
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed raw file 'Hawaii Tourism Data (from DBEDT Data Warehouse) (1).csv' (Hawaii Dept. of Business, Economic Development & Tourism data warehouse export), 1999-2021, broken out by visitor category (air, hotel-only, etc.) and island. Repo also has HawaiiLOS.sql (analysis queries) and derived Excel outputs: avg_los.xlsx, first_time_los.xlsx, repeat_los.xlsx, first_time_repeat_los_yearly.xlsx, YoY_visitors.xlsx, YoY_islands.xlsx — i.e. average length-of-stay split by first-time vs. repeat visitor, by year and by island. References a companion Kaggle dataset 'hawaii-travel-length-of-trip'.
candidates.why_useful: We already hold Hawaii DBEDT visitor stats as 'the only public party-size series' — this repo's committed CSV covers a longer span (1999-2021 vs whatever vintage we pulled) and, more importantly, has length-of-stay decomposed by first-time vs. repeat visitor and by island, which is new granularity directly on gap #20 (length-of-stay / party-size proxies) and is a Hawaii-like template that could be replicated for other STR-heavy island destinations.
candidates.size_hint: one CSV + several small xlsx outputs
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Hawaii DBEDT visitor stats (partial overlap) - this version is longer-history and has first-time/repeat LOS splits we don't currently have

candidates.name: hawaii-tourism-los-calculator
candidates.what_it_holds: Web app (importData.js loads a CSV into MongoDB) built around the same 'Hawaii Tourism Data (from DBEDT Data Warehouse)' source (1999-2021) as the danielnaqvi repo above; computes min/max average length-of-stay by visitor category and location/island. Raw CSV file is referenced by name but not clearly persisted in git (loaded into a database instead), so treat as a method/app rather than a guaranteed data mirror.
candidates.why_useful: Second independent implementation over the same DBEDT length-of-stay dataset; useful mainly as confirmation the dataset exists and as an alternate ingestion script if the danielnaqvi CSV is incomplete.

candidates.name: dr-tourism-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Single index.html file titled 'Dominican Republic tourism statistics dashboard'; repo tree shows no separate data files, README, or documented source. Could not confirm whether figures are drawn from Banco Central de la Republica Dominicana (BCRD) tourism releases, hard-coded, or AI-generated placeholder numbers. One commit, no contributors.
candidates.why_useful: If the embedded numbers do trace to BCRD's published monthly visitor-arrival series, this would be a quick pointer to DR travel-volume data (gap #7 region), but the single-file, single-commit shape and lack of source documentation makes this unverified — flagging for a human to open the HTML and check whether it cites real BCRD figures.

candidates.name: liming_bequia_dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: 'An interactive tourism dashboard for The Liming Bequia featuring visitor arrivals, market trends, seasonal patterns, and competitive analysis' for Bequia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines (a small Eastern Caribbean island). Description notes it was 'Built with Manus' (an AI app-builder), which raises real risk the underlying visitor-arrival/market-trend figures are AI-generated/synthetic rather than sourced from CTO or St. Vincent's tourism authority. Client/server/shared folder structure but no visible README data-source citation.
candidates.why_useful: Eastern Caribbean island-level tourism data is otherwise absent from our holdings, so if the numbers are real (sourced from the St. Vincent & Grenadines Tourism Authority or CTO) this would be a novel small-market data point; but the 'Built with Manus' provenance means this needs verification before any use, so it is flagged low/unverified rather than excluded.
candidates.geography: Bequia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines

candidates.name: Bahamas-Ministry-of-Tourism-COVID-Survey
candidates.what_it_holds: React + Semantic UI frontend for a COVID-19 travel survey the Bahamas Ministry of Tourism issued to travelers, from 2021. No survey results/response data appear to be committed - this is the survey-collection app itself, not a dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Historical curiosity only; confirms the Bahamas Ministry of Tourism ran a traveler survey app but the repo contains no response microdata. Not directly usable but shows the kind of instrument that might have public aggregate results published elsewhere (worth a human follow-up on the Ministry's own site).

notes: This modality (web search) was largely broken for this run: (1) WebSearch reported its session-wide budget (200/200) already exhausted before any of my queries ran, so I got zero real WebSearch results. (2) DuckDuckGo HTML/lite both served CAPTCHA challenge pages to WebFetch on every query - no results ever rendered. (3) Bing via WebFetch ignored 'site:github.com' filters and quoted-phrase operators entirely, instead returning generic top-authority pages for the topic words (Wikipedia/Britannica/cruise-line marketing sites for 'caribbean', github.com's own homepage/login/signup pages whenever the literal word 'github' appeared in the query, and once a completely unrelated 'workout routines' result set for an ICT/turismo query) - i.e. the WebFetch->Bing pipeline appears to summarize a served page that doesn't reflect the actual query, so Bing was unusable for site-restricted or GitHub-specific searches. (4) Marginalia and Ecosia both blocked/rate-limited the fetch outright. Given that, I fell back to the documented `gh search repos` escape hatch, which DID work (with two transient 403 'shared rate limit' bounces that cleared on retry) and produced every real candidate in this report. Recommend future scouts on this modality go straight to `gh search repos` rather than burning calls on search-engine WebFetch, since the search-engine path returned literally zero usable GitHub links across ~15 attempts. Substantively: this theme is sparse on GitHub - Costa Rica/Puerto Rico/Bahamas/Dominican Republic/CTO tourism data is dominated by tiny student/portfolio dashboard projects, most without committed real data; the two genuine hits (Costa Rica ICT parser, Hawaii DBEDT length-of-stay CSV) are both worth pulling. I did not find anything for Puerto Rico Tourism Company, CTO (Caribbean Tourism Organization) aggregate statistics, or Bahamas/Jamaica/Barbados beyond the items listed - a follow-up scout with working web search should specifically retry 'Puerto Rico Tourism Company visitor arrivals data.gov.pr' and CTO's own open-data portal for GitHub mirrors.
